discoveries.name: Neutralisation
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Acid + base → salt + water. The H⁺ from the acid and the OH⁻ from the base become water; what is left is a salt.

discoveries.name: Acid meets metal oxide
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Metal oxides are bases: they neutralise acids to make a salt and water, usually needing warmth.

discoveries.name: Acid meets carbonate
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Every carbonate fizzes in acid, giving a salt, water and carbon dioxide. Limewater turning milky is the test for that gas.

discoveries.name: Metal dissolves in acid
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series push hydrogen out of acids. The more reactive the metal, the faster it fizzes.

discoveries.name: Nitric acid attacks copper
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Copper and silver are too unreactive to give hydrogen, but nitric acid is an oxidiser: it dissolves them and gives off nitrogen oxide instead.

discoveries.name: Precipitation
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Two clear solutions swap partners, and if one new pair cannot dissolve it appears as a cloud of solid: a precipitate. Chemists use the colours to identify metal ions.

discoveries.name: Metal meets non-metal
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: A hot metal and a non-metal join directly into a salt: the simplest way to make a compound.

discoveries.name: Metal burns in air
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Heated in air, most metals join with oxygen to make an oxide.

discoveries.name: Displacement (more metals)
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: A more reactive metal pushes a less reactive one out of its salt. The less reactive metal coats the more reactive one.

discoveries.name: Thermal decomposition
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Heat breaks carbonates into oxides and carbon dioxide, hydroxides into oxides and water, and nitrates into oxides, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

discoveries.name: Water of crystallisation
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Many crystals hold water molecules in their structure. Heating drives the water out; adding water back puts it in again.

discoveries.name: Crystals take up water
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Dry salts grab water molecules back into their crystals, often changing colour and giving out heat.

discoveries.name: Oxides and water
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Metal oxides in water make alkalis; non-metal oxides in water make acids. That is why acid rain forms from sulfur and nitrogen oxides.

discoveries.name: Making an acid from its salt
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Hot sulfuric acid drives a more volatile acid out of its salt. This is how hydrochloric and nitric acid were first made.

discoveries.name: Rotten eggs
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Sulfides in acid give hydrogen sulfide, the gas that smells of rotten eggs. It is toxic, so do this in a draught.

discoveries.name: Test for ammonium
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Ammonium salts warmed with an alkali give off ammonia, which turns damp red litmus blue.

discoveries.name: Another catalyst
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Manganese dioxide splits hydrogen peroxide just as yeast does, and is not used up.

discoveries.name: Esterification
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: An acid and an alcohol join, losing water, to make an ester. Esters smell of fruit: pear drops, bananas, pineapples.

discoveries.name: Splitting an ester
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Alkali breaks an ester back into an alcohol and the salt of the acid. With fats, this makes soap.

discoveries.name: Oxidising alcohols
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids; secondary alcohols give ketones. Wine left open turns to vinegar this way.

discoveries.name: Fermentation
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide when there is no oxygen. It is how bread rises and how drinks are brewed.

discoveries.name: Breaking down sugars
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Acid and heat split big sugars into small ones: starch into glucose, sucrose into glucose and fructose.

discoveries.name: Soap making
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Oil and lye make soap and glycerol. People have made soap this way for over 4000 years.

discoveries.name: Polymerisation
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Small molecules (monomers) link into long chains (polymers). Every plastic is made this way.

discoveries.name: Combustion (organic)
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Anything made of carbon and hydrogen burns in oxygen to carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy.

discoveries.name: Smelting
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Carbon pulls the oxygen out of a metal oxide, leaving the metal. Zinc, lead and tin have been made this way for thousands of years.

discoveries.name: Freeing a halogen
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: An oxidiser takes electrons from chloride, bromide or iodide ions and frees the element: green chlorine, red-brown bromine, violet iodine.

discoveries.name: Chromate and dichromate
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Yellow chromate turns orange dichromate in acid, and back again in alkali: one of the prettiest equilibria in chemistry.

discoveries.name: Metals in alcohols
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Reactive metals fizz in alcohols as they do in water, more gently, giving hydrogen and an alkoxide.

discoveries.name: Carbide and acetylene
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Calcium carbide and water make acetylene, the gas that lit old miners' lamps.

discoveries.name: Double salts
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Two salts crystallising together into one crystal, like Mohr's salt and alum.

discoveries.name: Dehydrating alcohols
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Hot acid pulls water out of an alcohol, leaving a double bond: an alkene.

discoveries.name: Hydrating alkenes
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: An alkene and water join over an acid catalyst to make an alcohol. Industrial ethanol is made this way.

discoveries.name: The bromine test
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Orange bromine water goes colourless with an alkene, because bromine adds across the double bond.

discoveries.name: Haloalkanes
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: An alcohol's -OH group swaps for a halogen atom when it meets a hydrogen halide.

discoveries.name: Making amines
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Ammonia pushes the halogen off a haloalkane, giving an amine: an organic cousin of ammonia.

discoveries.name: Making amides
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Acids and ammonia join, losing water, to make amides like acetamide.

discoveries.name: Making ethers
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: Two alcohol molecules lose one water between them to make an ether. Diethyl ether was the first surgical anaesthetic.

discoveries.name: Strong acid frees a weak acid
discoveries.hint: One of the families of reactions that make the 1,700 compounds.
discoveries.fact: A strong acid hands its hydrogen to the salt of a weak acid, freeing the weak acid. This is how soap curdles in acid.
